speaker: Doctor
text:
Good morning, I see you are pregnant and experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any rash, stiff neck, or sensitivity to light?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP, and liver function tests.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC 15,000/μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, Platelets 200,000/μL. LIVER FUNCTION TESTS: AST Within normal limits, ALT Within normal limits, Bilirubin Within normal limits.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. The patient is currently pregnant, at her 30th week of gestation. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travels or contact with sick individuals. No known allergies.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies cough, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you noticed any nausea, vomiting, or muscle aches in addition to your headache and fever?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Liver Function Tests (LFTs).
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC 15,000/μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, Platelets 200,000/μL. LIVER FUNCTION TESTS: AST Within normal limits, ALT Within normal limits, Bilirubin Within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your elevated white blood cell count and the presence of fever, headache, and fatigue, have you noticed any eye pain with movement or blurred vision, which can indicate inflammation of the optic nerve?

REQUEST TEST: Visual Acuity and Visual Field Examination.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you experienced any abdominal pain, particularly in the upper right quadrant, or any changes in your urine color?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Direct Antiglobulin Test (Coombs).
REQUEST IMAGES: Hepatobiliary Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Clear, WBC 0-5 /HPF, RBC 0-2 /HPF, Protein Negative, Glucose Negative. Direct Antiglobulin Test (Coombs): Not performed in provided data. Hepatobiliary Ultrasound: Not performed in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your symptoms of fever, headache, and malaise combined with leukocytosis but normal liver and eye exams, have you recently traveled to areas where tick-borne illnesses like Lyme disease or Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever are common, or do you recall any tick bites?

REQUEST TEST: Lyme Serology (ELISA/Western Blot) and Rickettsial Serology.
REQUEST TEST: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR) and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lyme Serology (ELISA/Western Blot): Not performed in provided data. Rickettsial Serology: Not performed in provided data. Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR): Not performed in provided data. C-Reactive Protein (CRP): Not performed in provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the recent serologies for Lyme and Rickettsia were not available in your results, have you noticed any muscle weakness, tingling in your hands or feet, or confusion?

REQUEST TEST: Electrolytes, Magnesium, and Phosphate levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your recent brain imaging and electrolyte panels are normal, have you noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, dark urine, or pale stools?

REQUEST TEST: Total Bilirubin, Fractional Bilirubin, and Urobilinogen.

Please let me know if you have had any recent exposure to raw meat or unpasteurized dairy products.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Have you consumed unpasteurized milk or soft cheeses recently? This is crucial as normal bilirubin helps rule out classic listeriosis, but other atypical presentations must be considered.

REQUEST TEST: Listeria Monocytogenes PCR and Serum IgM/IgG antibodies.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Atypical presentation)
